learning: Reduced base speed and adjusted PID gains to improve steering precision and reduce oscillations, expecting better track completion and stability.
notes: Kept geometry unchanged as it supports good sensing and stability. Controller tuned with lower speed and adjusted PID gains to address off-track failures and oscillations seen in telemetry.
rationale: The previous iteration's geometry with 7 sensors, sensor size 0.016, and wheel track 0.15 provides good line detection resolution and turning stability, as intended. The race telemetry shows the robot still fails to complete the track, going off track early on both oval and s-bend tracks. The main issues appear to be controller tuning: the base speed is too high for precise steering, and the PID gains need adjustment to reduce oscillations and improve tracking accuracy. I reduce base speed from 0.11 to 0.09 to allow more precise control and increase kp from 1.0 to 1.2 to strengthen proportional correction. I reduce ki from 0.06 to 0.04 to avoid integral windup and reduce kd from 0.015 to 0.01 to smooth steering response. Sensor weights remain symmetric and balanced for the 7 sensors. I keep the geometry unchanged to isolate controller tuning effects. I request the same measurements as before plus steering_oscillation and control_effort to better evaluate controller performance and stability.
